subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Grind Size Science
description: A 60-second lesson on Grind Size Science.

hook.text: Grind size controls how fast water extracts flavor. Get it wrong and no technique can save the cup.

buildup.text: Fine grinds expose more surface area, extracting faster. Coarse grinds extract slower.

discovery.text: Espresso needs powder-fine grinds. French press needs coarse, like sea salt. Each method demands its own size.

twist.text: Cheap blade grinders shatter beans into random sizes—some over-extract, some under-extract in the same brew.

climax.text: Burr grinders crush beans to uniform size. Consistency is the single biggest upgrade for home coffee quality.

punchline.text: Uniform grind, uniform extraction, delicious cup. It starts here.

quiz.question: Why are burr grinders preferred over blade grinders?
options: They produce uniform grind size for even extraction

details.summary: Grind size determines how quickly water extracts flavors from coffee. Fine grinds expose more surface area for fast extraction in espresso. Coarse grinds slow extraction for immersion methods like French press. Particle size consistency is as important as the size itself.
details.whyItMatters: Grind size is the easiest variable to adjust and has the biggest impact on flavor. Getting it right is the fastest way to improve any brewing method.
takeaways: Fine grinds extract fast, suited for short brew methods
Coarse grinds extract slowly, suited for immersion brewing
Uniform particle size prevents simultaneous over and under extraction

faq.question: Why do burr grinders produce better coffee than blade grinders?
faq.answer: Burr grinders crush beans between two abrasive surfaces to produce uniform particles. Blade grinders chop randomly, creating a mix of fine dust and large chunks. This inconsistency causes simultaneous over and under extraction, muddying the flavor.

faq.question: What grind size should each brew method use?
faq.answer: Espresso needs fine, almost powdery grounds. Pour-over uses medium like sea salt. French press requires coarse like raw sugar. Cold brew uses extra coarse. Each method's contact time with water determines the ideal grind size.
